text:
A: Hiya, you alright? I'm Daniel.
B: Hi. Erm, Bethany. Hi.
A: Nice to meet you, Bethany. How are you finding these, are you on your last one?
B: Yeah, I think so. They're alright. I'm not very good at the starting bit.
A: Ha, no one is, honestly. Where are you calling from?
B: Basingstoke.
A: Ah, okay. I'm Peterborough. I've only been to Basingstoke for a training day, and I spent most of it lost on a roundabout.
B: Yeah, that happens a lot, sorry.
A: Not your fault! So what do you do?
B: Erm, IT service desk, second-line, at an insurance company. Password resets, Outlook, people's laptops not connecting. That sort of thing.
A: Oh, you're a hero then. Our IT lot get rung every time a scanner stops on the warehouse floor. I'm operations manager at a distribution centre, so when the system goes down at two in the morning I'm the one ringing someone like you, a bit stressed.
B: Ha, yeah. I don't mind the stressed ones though. If you stay calm they sort of calm down with you.
A: That's a skill, that. Honestly. I've got supervisors who can't do that. Do you enjoy it?
B: Erm, mostly. I'd quite like something more technical eventually. Like Microsoft 365 admin, or infrastructure. Less on the phones. I've been meaning to start a course, Azure fundamentals, for, erm, about six months.
A: Six months is nothing. I said I'd do an MBA about four years ago, and I've still not decided. Is it something work would pay for?
B: I think so, yeah. My manager mentioned it. I just haven't, sort of, done it.
A: If it's any help, what I do is put it in the calendar like a meeting. An hour on a Tuesday, blocked out. Sounds sad, but it works. My wife says I'd schedule a sneeze.
B: That's actually a good idea. I might try that.
A: Go on. What do you do outside work, then?
B: Reading, mostly. Fantasy, and cosy mysteries. And walks on the canal. I keep trying Couch to 5K, but I've restarted week three about four times.
A: Week three's the hard one, everybody says that. I do parkrun most Saturdays, Ferry Meadows. You get all sorts, people walking it, people with buggies. There's one in Basingstoke, I think, you could just walk it the first time.
B: Oh, maybe. I don't really like doing things with loads of people watching.
A: Nobody's watching, honestly, they're all too busy dying. Do you live with anyone?
B: My partner, Dan. And our cat, Biscuit.
A: Dan! Good name. Strong name.
B: Ha, yeah. He's a shift manager, in a warehouse, actually.
A: No way. What's his shift pattern like?
B: Erm, it changes a lot. Earlies, lates. We have a calendar on the fridge.
A: Sounds about right. Tell him from me, the calendar on the fridge is the only thing holding it together. My wife's a teacher, so she gets all the holidays and I get none, it's a constant negotiation.
B: Yeah. We went to Edinburgh last year for a weekend, which was nice, because we both actually had the time off.
A: Edinburgh's brilliant. Did you go up Arthur's Seat?
B: Erm, sort of halfway. Then we went to a bookshop instead.
A: Ha, honestly, that's the right call. I did it with the dog and he—
